newsitem.title: CANADA: INSTANT VIEW - Canada October unemployment.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Canada October unemployment.

text.p: Following are reactions to unemployment data released by Statistics Canada on Friday.

October unemployment rose to 10.0 percent versus 9.9 percent in September. Employment climbed 42,000 to 13.72 million. A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unemployment rate to drop to 9.7 percent in October.

Douglas Porter, senior economist, Nesbitt Burns Inc -- "I think the big story in this data is how strongly the labor force continues to grow...The job gains have not been sufficient to mop up the increase in the labor force.
"This report is sort of right down the middle. I think it doesn't rule (a rate cut) out," Porter added.

Mark Mullins, senior economist, Midland Walwyn Capital -- "If you look at the headline number, you've got a slight increase in the unemployment number...But actually this report is exactly what a guy looking for growth wants to see -- most of the growth in the private sector, most of the jobs full-time.
"This report on the face of it, at least to me, argues against the bank moving."

Mark Chandler, senior economist, Goldman Sachs Canada -- "(It was) sort of mixed with the unemployment rate going up and the employment gain being strong. But I think the thing that really carries the weight is the employment gain.
"I think the bank will still ease today (to ratify market expectation and to offset the effect of a stronger dollar)."
